column2: req_desc

Accounts and sessions
Visitors create an account with an email and password, sign in and sign out, and every archive page and API call except the public ones named in API needs a session that lasts as set in Business rules.

Owner-only records
A roll, log entry, scan, frame, calibration, pinned reading, original download or loupe reading that belongs to another account answers not-found exactly as an unknown id does, including ids inside request bodies.

Rolls
You create and edit rolls with name, stock, format, EI, push or pull, reciprocity exponent, development note, kind (normal or test) and an optional linked test-roll curve, validated as in Business rules.

Shooting log entries
Each roll holds shooting-log entries keyed by a unique frame-counter number, with aperture, shutter, metered EV, note and a misfire flag, and the server rejects unmarked apertures and shutter strings it cannot parse.

Relative exposure
Every entry reports its relative exposure in stops and in relative log H, derived on every read from the roll's current EI and reciprocity exponent, with apertures read as exact third-stop values, exposures longer than one second corrected for reciprocity failure and rounding as defined in Business rules.

Note and title limits
Exposure notes, development notes and frame titles have published character limits that the form and the server enforce identically, counting each Unicode code point as one character.

Log a roll while shooting
The film photographer signs in, starts a roll from the Log screen, logs exposures one after another including a misfire and a long night exposure, and sees each entry with its computed stops in the roll's shooting log.

Stored only after storage confirms
A strip upload answers success, and the scan appears as Stored, only after the server has confirmed that the object in storage has the declared byte size and SHA-256.

Originals kept as submitted
The stored object and the original download are byte-identical to the upload, with the same SHA-256, and the derived 8-bit previews are stored separately.

One copy per strip
Uploading bytes that are already a scan on the same roll stores nothing new and answers duplicate with the existing scan id, and of simultaneous identical uploads exactly one is stored.

Upload a developed strip
The home developer opens a roll, chooses a strip scan with its DPI and first edge number, uploads it, sees it listed as Stored with its size and checksum, and opens its strip workspace.

PNG and TIFF judged by content
Strip uploads are accepted only when the bytes begin with a PNG or TIFF signature, whatever the file name or declared content type, and only in the pixel formats and TIFF layouts that Business rules allows.

Size and pixel limits before decoding
Uploads above the byte limit, and images whose PNG header or first TIFF image directory declares dimensions beyond the published pixel limits, are refused before any pixels are decoded or any frame detection runs.

All-or-nothing uploads
A refused, failed or interrupted upload leaves neither a scan record nor any stored object, so a roll never points at a missing negative.

Honest storage outage
When storage is unreachable, uploads and every action that reads an original are refused with the storage error and banner, while rolls, notes, alignments, frames and pinned readings stay readable, and stay editable wherever no original is needed.

Read the archive during an outage
With storage down, the film photographer signs in, sees the storage banner, opens a roll and reads its counters, contact sheet entries, shooting notes and pinned readings.

Clear-light calibration
Marking a clear-light patch calibrates a scan so that density is the base-10 log of the patch's mean linear value over the point's linear value, with linear values read from the stored original at full bit depth through its own transfer as defined in Business rules.

Step-wedge calibration
Marking a scanned 21-step wedge calibrates a scan through a piecewise-linear fit of its linear step means at the published nominal step densities, and a wedge whose steps do not darken in order is rejected.

Frame detection and width flags
Find frames locates frames between the brighter inter-frame gaps of the linear values at the format's published pitch and the scan's DPI, drops cut frames at the strip ends, inserts blank slots for unexposed frames, and flags any frame outside the published width tolerance until it is accepted or nudged into range.

Boundary nudges
Moving a frame's left or right edge saves new scan-pixel boundaries and recomputes that frame's density, its width flag and the scan's base plus fog, and edges that leave the scan or overlap a neighbour are rejected.

Keyboard frame handles
Every frame edge handle is a focusable slider with a visible gold focus outline that the arrow keys nudge and Enter saves, and flagged frames can be accepted by keyboard.

Counters match the contact sheet
A roll's four counters (detected, aligned, unexposed, unmatched notes) on the archive index, the roll page and the API always equal what its contact sheet and shooting log show, immediately after any nudge, log change or alignment change.

Alignment proposal
Propose alignment scores every offset from −2 to +2, with and without one slip after a note, by the rank correlation between logged exposure and measured frame density, excluding misfires and unexposed frames, and proposes a slip only under the published margin and tie-break rules.

Accepting and overriding alignment
Saving an alignment stores an offset, an optional slip after a note and per-note overrides that always win, records whether it is proposed or manual, and wherever an override or a manual alignment applies the screen shows Manual.

Roll and scan states
Scans move from stored to calibrated, framed and aligned, normal rolls move from logging to developed and aligned, test rolls move between logging and curve-ready, and every out-of-order action answers its published conflict.

Keyboard alignment dialog
Using the keyboard alone, the Override alignment dialog opens and works in its published Tab order, Tab and Shift+Tab wrap inside it, Escape closes it, and focus returns to its opener.

Align a roll's notes
The home developer calibrates and frames each strip, proposes an alignment, sets a slip or overrides one note to a different frame, saves, and sees every frame paired with its note and the roll marked Aligned.

Density from the stored original
A loupe reading at any scan-pixel point returns gross density, net density above base plus fog, relative log H and zone for its sample cell, computed from the stored original's linear values with the scan's current calibration.

Densitometer Loupe
Pointer or keyboard focus on the strip opens a square loupe at four times magnification around the sample cell, showing net density, gross density and relative log H in that order, with the curve panel's dot and zone label following it, the arrow keys moving it one cell and Shift+arrows moving it eight.

Pinned readings
Enter or click pins the current cell, the server recomputes its density from the stored original's linear values and stores it with the calibration it used, and the readings list and the canvas marker show the server's value, which equals the loupe's.

Pin readings on a frame
The home developer calibrates a strip, moves the loupe over a frame, pins a reading, and finds it listed under that frame beside the frame's shooting note.

Characteristic curve figures
A test roll with enough aligned bracket frames draws its characteristic curve and reports base plus fog, speed point, contrast index, frames used and stop span, as defined in Business rules.

Meter bias
A normal roll linked to a curve-ready test roll reports its meter bias, the median difference between curve-inverted and logged stops over its aligned frames, to the nearest 0.1 stop.

Read a film's curve
The home developer aligns the seeded bracket test roll, opens Curves, reads its curve and contrast index, links it to a normal roll, and reads that roll's meter bias.

Archive index
The archive shows each roll, newest first, as a print of its strongest frame with stock, EI and its four counters, in uneven arrangements where no two neighbouring rolls share one.

Strip workspace layouts
The strip workspace shows the published order and arrangement at 375, 768 and 1280 pixels wide, with no horizontal page scrolling.

Find a frame with its notes
The film photographer opens the archive, picks a roll, opens a frame from its contact sheet, gives it a title, and reads its shooting note and pinned readings beside the negative.

Run manifest and health
The app installs, builds and serves from /app/run.json on the published port and answers the health check as specified.

Server boundary
The server is same-origin only, enforces the published body limits, refuses cross-origin writes, and never serves source, credentials or the environment.

Credentials from the environment
Every database and storage credential and endpoint is read at start from the published environment variables, never hard-coded and never sent to the browser.

Darkroom look
As described in Visual design, every screen fills a deep bottle-green ground edge to edge, with gold Host Grotesk text in tabular figures, square corners, uneven print arrangements on a twelve-column grid and airy spacing.

Negatives stay negatives
Every scan, frame crop and loupe view draws the film in its true negative state through the exact gold-on-green tint in Business rules, with hard-edged pixels in the loupe, and no screen offers a positive conversion as the default view.

Two prints in darkness
The landing page shows, in the published arrangement, the wordmark, three links, the Open archive rectangle, a large procedural negative print, a small dimmed procedural step-wedge print, the headline and the muted sentence, and once the user is signed in the large print shows their latest aligned frame.

Loupe and curve motion
As described in Motion and effects, the loupe opens as a square shutter and closes faster, the curve dot glides to its new place, the loupe tracks the pointer without lag, nothing loops decoratively, and reduced motion removes the shutter and the glide entirely.

Announced feedback
Every async action shows its published pending, success, field-error and outage copy and announces it through the Activity live region, and the storage banner is an alert.

Live exposure preview
The Log form and every inline entry edit show an Exposure preview that recomputes stops and log H in place on every change of roll, aperture, shutter or metered EV, reciprocity included, without a request, and equals the server's figures once logged.

Announced upload progress and outcome
While a strip uploads, a progressbar tracks the bytes actually sent, the Activity region announces exactly the pending copy and then one final outcome, and focus lands on the stored or existing strip or on the invalid field, as qualified in Feedback states.

Bounded refusal of crafted scans
The crafted PNGs and TIFFs listed in Business rules are refused with their published field copy within 5 seconds, writing no record and no object, while the health check keeps answering within 1 second.

Serialised boundary nudges
Concurrent nudges on one scan are applied one at a time, so of two that would overlap only together exactly one succeeds, a nudge to one edge never changes the other, and base plus fog, net densities and counters equal a recomputation from the final edges.

Curves follow every edit
Curve figures, readiness, meter bias and every reading's log H and zone are derived on read and follow every entry, EI, reciprocity exponent, frame, calibration and alignment edit, while a pinned reading's point, gross, net, calibration and entry never change after pinning, as qualified in Business rules.

Published landing routes
Signed-out deep links return to the exact requested route after sign-in or sign-up when the next value is safe and to the archive otherwise, and every roll, log and sign-out action lands on its published route.

Latest loupe cell wins
The loupe readout, curve dot and zone show only the reading for the cell the loupe currently rests on, discarding late responses for cells it has left, and a pin always stores that current cell.

Versioned alignment saves
Saving an alignment names the version it was based on, a save against any other version answers the stale-alignment conflict, and of simultaneous saves on one version exactly one succeeds, as qualified in Business rules.

Request-scoped records
Every response and screen comes only from the requesting session's account, so concurrent requests from two accounts never cross and a second account signing in after Sign out without a reload sees only its own records.

Expired-session drafts
When Log exposure or Save note meets an expired session, the unsent fields are kept, the browser goes to sign in, and the same account gets every field back with nothing sent until it presses the button again, while any other account starts clean.

Released when an upload is cut off
An upload cut off mid-body leaves no object and releases its duplicate guard and database connection within 2 seconds, so the same bytes re-uploaded at once are stored, while the health check keeps answering.

Honest refusals during an outage
During a storage outage a refused edge nudge springs back to its saved column, a refused pin draws no marker and lists nothing, and a frame update that changes an edge saves no part of itself, title included.

Loupe by touch
On touch, a first tap on the strip opens the loupe on that cell, a tap on another cell moves it without pinning, a second tap on the same cell pins it, and vertical swipes from the strip still scroll the page.

Owner-only derived surfaces
Curve from test roll options, Curves, the hero's latest aligned frame, Recent exposures and each roll's strongest frame are built only from the signed-in account's records, even when another account owns a newer record with the same name.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve keys and _schema run-manifest-v1, and its commands call Python tools inside /app/.venv by path or as python -m.

/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md names every shipped package and the bundled Host Grotesk font with its licence; shipped packages are the production dependency tree installed into /app/.venv from the production requirements, excluding development and test groups.
Every shipped package and font uses one of MIT, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, ISC, PSF-2.0, HPND, MIT-CMU, LGPL-3.0-or-later or OFL-1.1.
The only datastores are the provided PostgreSQL and MinIO, with no SQLite files, no other servers, and no scan bytes written to local disk beyond the life of one request.
Pages load no script, style or font from any other origin, and Host Grotesk is bundled and served by the app.
The provided service definitions and their seeded configuration are left unchanged.
